title: Tsunami: Long or Strong, Get Gone, then return
version: Get Ready (NEMA) tsunami page, its NZ Sign Language version (nzsl.getready.govt.nz/emergency/tsunami), the Get Ready large-print tsunami copy (08-tsunami-lp-en-dec24.pdf) and NEMA's Civil Defence consistent-messages page 'Response: What to do during a tsunami' (civildefence.govt.nz), read 19 Nov 2026, no review date shown on any web page
sourceNote: The sites block direct download, so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote short exact sentences (long ones in pieces, rejoined); about 25 key lines (numbers, 'do not', times, depths) were confirmed EXACT in a second read, but small wording slips are possible and the order of a few lines in Section D is the tool's. Four labelled sections: A main page, B Sign Language page (adds headings, the hikoi practice walk, the warning-channel, informal-source and lake lists, and the 'if your property is damaged' lines), C large-print copy (the only Get Ready copy of the shore warning-sign list: strong/long earthquake, sudden sea-level rise or fall, loud or unusual noises from the sea), D Civil Defence response messages (warning types, evacuate-now vs prepare-to-evacuate, driving, grab bag, and the only boat / at-sea advice). Left out: navigation, download and poster labels, te reo Maori poster text, linked videos and East Coast LAB sheets, and the civildefence.govt.nz 'Get Tsunami Ready' campaign page. Not captured: the main page's bulleted lists (the fetch tool showed lead-ins like 'any of the following' with no list after them; Sections B and C fill these), and the rest of the large-print PDF. Oddities and gaps: (1) the main page and large-print copy list three shore signs including noises, but the Sign Language page's shore sentence names only sea-level change and a strong or long earthquake, no noises; (2) the earthquake sign is worded three ways: 'long earthquake that lasts more than a minute' (Get Ready), 'weak rolling earthquake that lasts a minute or more' (Civil Defence) and 'long, weak, rolling earthquake that lasts a minute or more' (lake list), so exactly one minute is ambiguous; (3) the 'after' lists differ slightly: the main page says 'Listen to the radio or follow your ... Group online' and 'If there was an earthquake', the Sign Language page says 'Follow your ... Group online' and 'If you felt an earthquake'; (4) after-tsunami water advice is 'Stay away ... for at least 24 hours' on Get Ready but only 'Be cautious in and around' (no time) on the Civil Defence page; (5) Civil Defence says the first wave may not be the largest and activity lasts several hours, which Get Ready does not say; (6) warning sources differ (Get Ready: NEMA website, radio, TV, EMA, siren, phone, text, loud hailer; Civil Defence: civildefence.govt.nz and Twitter @NZCivilDefence, which looks dated); (7) no NEMA page found mentions vertical evacuation or upper floors: the only 'can't get out' guidance is 'Even if you can't get out of your evacuation zone, go as far or as high as you can. Every metre makes a difference.' (vertical evacuation advice exists only on regional sites such as WREMO, not captured); (8) boat advice is only on the Civil Defence sector page, not on Get Ready; it gives 50 metres depth and a ten-minute beach-and-walk rule but says nothing about small boats already in deep water beyond 'continue to head to deeper water', and the 'leave your boats' line for marinas sits under the activity advisory; (9) no guidance on people who cannot walk, run or cycle beyond 'Use of vehicles ... limited to ... mobility impairments, including wheelchair users', and the Drop, Cover and Hold variants for those who can't get up. Saving the Get Ready page as a PDF into sources/ would make checking exact.
status: Reviewer: 3 instructions missed (incl. how to Drop, Cover and Hold) and 15 findings, all fixed. 121 of 121 quotes exact (web copy).
